This soundfont will nearly support Yamaha XG Drum mapping configuration. But not all the GS/XG Voices (Instruments). Besides of Roland GS SFX and some few special new additions by me.
**As it turned out while using Yamaha S-YXG50 VSTi, Yamaha XG Soundset is more used to access various instruments by CC#32 (Bank Select LSB) messages rather than traditional CC#0 (MSB) messages used in GS. SF2 format does not support that. It is only functional in Most significant level only. So the hardwork goes on and on starting from repatching the old 90's Yamaha MusicSoft MIDI files.

I really can't say that I created this Soundfont.  All I did was put it together.  I took instruments from different soundfonts and put them into this font.

Some of the instruments are from the 8 meg soundfont that comes with the SBLive! card.  I pretty much started with that font, took out all the percusives and sound effects, and all the un-neccessary instruments.

Most of the percusives are from the original FF7.sf2 font, but part of 'FF7 Percussive' kit came from Jari Huttunen's  Timber Soundfont.

Several of the melodic instruments (most of the woodwinds,  and a few others) also came from Timber.

The percussive organ in 'Still More Fighting' came from some SoundFonts I downloaded at Hammersound.net

Most of the instruments in banks 1-8 came from the original FF7.sf2, along with the tubular bells and Electric Piano.

I'm pretty sure I've explained where most of the instruments are.  A great thanks goes out to all the authors of the soundfonts that I borrowed instruments from.

[differences in version 1.1]

-Added a really cool Overdriven guitar from Timber to J-E-N-O-V-A (finally fixing that crappy Synth Vox instrument)

-Added a few of the instruments from the original FF7 soundfont (made it sound better.)

-Added a couple better pianos.

-Fixed the FF7 Percussives.  Now the Shinra theme sounds right.

[Differences in version 1.2]

-Fixed the Oboe volume problem.  Now it doesn't sound overpowering in 'The Highwind Takes to the Skies'

-Added the original Synth bass for 'The Great Northern Cave', because the one I had didn't sound good.

-Added better strings for 'Hurry, Faster!' and 'Reunion', now they sound more like they should.

[Differences in Version 1.3]

-Fixed an error where 'Honey Bee Manor' used 'J-E-N-O-V-A''s guitar and sounded pretty bad.

-Added The Percussion Organ from Sam Slight's FF8 DLS (version 1.35) for 'Still More Fighting'

-Removed the Clarinet that served as the square wave in 'Still More Fighting', re-assigned that to the 'J-E-N-O-V-A' Overdriven guitar.

[Differences in Version 1.4]

- added the brass ensemble in 'J-E-N-O-V-A'.  Before, that instrument was so quiet it sounded like it wasn't playing.

- put in an entirely new main drum kit, basically taken from Unison.  (The snares are from Atomic, and the 2 instruments in 'Shinra, Inc' are from the original FF7 Font.)

- The Square wave in 'Still More Fighting' was finally replaced with an actual square wave.  (taken from Samuel Slights FF7 patch.)

-Added a nice new slow strings, compliments of Samuel Slight's FF7 XG patch.

-Added a nice new Oboe, from Unison.

-Added a nice new Fingered bass (a YAMAHA TRB-5)

-Replaced the Over driven Guitar in 'J-E-N-O-V-A' with an instrument that sounds much more like the one in the PSX version.

CHANGED FOR 1.41

-I don't think this warrants the release of a whole new version 
(hence the 1.41 instead of 1.5), but I recorded samples of the YAMAHA 
SoftSynth's Percussion Organ (That really cool one it uses in Still 
More Fighting) and put it into my SoundFont.

[Differences in Version 1.5]

-Changed the Sqaure Wave for 'Still More Fighting'.

[Differences in verion 1.6]

The only change made between version 1.5 and 1.6 is the incorporation of lb2.sf2 into the ff7.sf2 file.  'One Winged Angel' 
will now play fine without having to load the lb2.sf2 file.  (Note:  I did not "fix" any of the "issues" with 'One Winged 
Angel', so don't expect it to sound more like the psx or better . . . it sounds the same as it did in previous versions of 
this SoundFont.)

info.ICMT:
I, stgiga, need to say a few things (about this 1GB bank): 

First off, Micasddsa didn't know why they made their original Beepbox Soundfont. It also had some issues, such as the pitch for everything being far too high, resulting in an ear-shriveling result. I, stgiga, fixed that using Polyphone, which ended up going well. I also remapped the stuff not in the 128 basic GM tones to Roland SC-8850 equivalents (like the FM Organ). Conveniently, too!
 The second issue was a lack of drums, which was fixed by implementing the drums from Zandro Reveille's OPL-3 GM Soundfont after ages of searching for usable drumkits. TheFatMan has a part in that equation. 
Third: Beepbox is MIT License, and Zandro's bank is Creative Commons ShareAlike, meaning that this is legitimate to use in a project. Micasddsa didn't realize this. 
This bank is thus under the ShareAlike Creative Commons license.

Fourth: Everything is only 1 layer, so OpenMPT is able to use it.
I hope you enjoy this! Stay safe!

info.ICOP: © 1999 ROLAND CORPORATION, 2018 mpj factory studios, quto, ecuador, RolandKnight, niltwill, stgiga
info.ICMT:
I'm stgiga. This is my merger of the fixed Yamaha Tyros 4 GM Soundfont by Milton Paredes with Thomas K's Roland JV-1010 GM Soundfont. The version of the Roland JV-1010 Soundfont used was 1.0 but with the better samples and preset attenuations copied from the first 1.1 release (the last one that kept the full sample rate), as well as the Drumkit presets added in that version. While the fixed version of the Yamaha Tyros 4 Soundfont was used, unused samples in the old version were implemented, and the preset layers exclusive to the old version were also added, but in a way that layered both the old and new versions of the presets involved. RolandKnight is the person who did the fixed version of Milton Paredes' Tyros 4 Soundfont, including stereo fixes that I improved. Also SFX and SC-8850 vocals were added via mapping the Tyros 4 SFX and Vocal Effects stuff to presets, including XG.

Do note that this duet bank is basically a 1-on-1 layering of the GM patches of the Yamaha Tyros 4 and the Roland JV-1010 that I did when I was bored. I never expected it to sound as realistic as it does (but it was a welcome surprise), in addition to being balanced extremely well (also a pleasant surprise). It is also under 1 gigabyte, which means that even users of Fluidsynth 1.x can load this, as well as anything else that supports 1 gigabyte or less due to limitations. It can fit as-is on a 99 minute CD, or when compressed can fit on a standard CD (assuming 7zip compression) with a decent amount of space left. It must be said that this bank is GM, unifying two devices into a duet, but purely. It isn't cheating when it comes down to the "two device" premise. Just the Yamaha Tyros 4 and Roland JV-1010 together in harmony. For those who try to port tunes to multiple platforms, this is an interesting target to do so. In addition, porting remixes to this can actually be considered further remixes due to it always being two devices in unity. This bank is also not a volume or polyphony monster, meaning that complicated tunes can be played easily. I hope you enjoy this fine release!  

Also, do what you want with this bank!

Thomas K. says:
All JV-1010 sounds were sampled from a real Roland JV-1010 hardware sound module.

And now I welcome you to the realistic wonderful world of Tyroland!
